rounds.name: Cold email that books calls
rounds.prompt: Write a cold email (max 110 words) to Mark, owner of Ace Plumbing in Ohio, selling an after-hours call answering service. Mention one specific pain point and end with a clear call to action.

columns.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
columns.prompt: Write a cold email (max 110 words) to Mark, owner of Ace Plumbing in Ohio...

result.text: Hi Mark, quick one: your Google listing says 'emergency plumbing' but calls after 6pm go to voicemail. We answer 24/7 and book jobs straight into your calendar. Worth a 10-minute call Thursday?

columns.reason: Short and clear, but no real hook.

columns.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
columns.prompt: Write a cold email (max 110 words) to Mark, owner of Ace Plumbing in Ohio...

result.text:
Subject: Missed calls after 6pm?

Hi Mark,

I noticed Ace Plumbing advertises emergency service, but evening calls hit voicemail. Most callers won't leave a message, they call the next plumber.

We set up an answering line that books jobs for you overnight. Typical result: 3-5 extra jobs a month.

Open to a 10-minute call this week?

Sam

columns.reason: Good subject line and a concrete number.

columns.name: Claude Opus 5.5
columns.prompt: Write a cold email (max 110 words) to Mark, owner of Ace Plumbing in Ohio...

result.text:
Subject: The 7pm call you missed

Mark,

A homeowner with a burst pipe at 7pm won't leave voicemail, they call the next name on Google. Your listing promises emergency service; your phone stops at 6.

We answer those calls, qualify them and drop the job into your calendar. No new staff.

One recovered job usually covers a month.

Worth 10 minutes Thursday at 4?

Sam

columns.reason: Vivid scenario, strong CTA with a time.

talk.title: SAMPLE: 3 AIs Write Cold Emails for a Plumber
talk.hook: Three AIs. One plumber. 2 seconds versus 12 seconds, and 40 times the price. Is the expensive AI actually better?
talk.contestants: In the budget corner, Haiku. In the middle, Sonnet. And the premium heavyweight, Opus. Same prompts, real answers, a blind judge.

rounds.intro: Round one. A cold email that actually books calls.
rounds.answers: Haiku is done in two seconds. Sonnet adds a subject line. Opus paints a burst pipe at 7pm.
rounds.scores: The judge gives the round to Opus, for the vivid scenario and a call to action with an actual time.
